text:
Meera: Heads up — I pushed a small instrumentation change to token-level metrics on staging. Adds per-kernel attribution + KV-prefetch tagging. Goal: split TTFT vs decode and see which kernel is dominating short prompt latency.

Tom: Nice. What did you add exactly?

Meera: Emitted two new OTEL attributes on the token span: `kernel.name` and `kvcache.prefetch` (values: `none|attempted|hit|miss`). Also added `kernel.exec_ms` per-kernel as discrete metrics (we sample 1% of requests by default).

Ashley: Can you paste the metric schema?

Meera: Sure — sample event payload:```
metric.redwood.token_latency {
  ttft_ms: 34,
  decode_ms: 22,
  kernel_conv_ms: 8,
  kernel_matmul_ms: 4,
  kvcache_prefetch: "attempted",
  kvcache_hit: "no",
  route: "chat-stream",
  model: "rw-v1-13b"
}
```

Jordan: Good. Sampling at 1% seems fine for storage, but is it enough to get stable per-route kernels? For low-traffic routes we'll be noisy.

Meera: Agreed. Plan: 1% global + route-based upsampling for routes in `per_route_watchlist` (~10 routes). We can tweak.

Nikhil: FYI I ran a quick A/B on staging earlier today. Baseline (no prefetch tagging) median TTFT on short prompts (<=32 tokens) = 26ms. With tagging + prefetch enabled, some runs show median 32ms. Raw traces point to kernel_conv_ms increasing.

Tom: Oof. Do you have an example trace?

Nikhil: Pasted anonymized trace below (short):
```
trace id: t-9b3f
span token 1: ttft 31ms (decode 20ms, kernel_conv 9ms, kernel_matmul 2ms)
span token 2: ttft 6ms  (decode 4ms, kernel_conv 1ms, kvcache hit)
```

Meera: That's interesting — kernel_conv up by ~50% for first token. Could be prefetch path adding overhead when it misclassifies sequence length and selects a microkernel with extra packing.

Ashley: Could this just be instrumentation overhead? Adding per-kernel exec_ms and OTEL attrs might change hot path timings.

Meera: I measured overhead with synthetic microbenchmarks — attribute emission is cheap (~0.1ms) when sampling, and we only emit for sampled requests. The regression seems larger than that.

Jordan: If prefetch logic triggers an extra memory copy or a different kernel path, that could explain the ~6ms delta. We saw similar effects when batching handshake changed last quarter.

Tom: Action items: 1) enable verbose kernel selector logs for 1% of staging requests (different sampling than the metric sampling) 2) add a dashboard panel showing kernel selection frequency vs TTFT for short prompts 3) run a narrow canary disabling prefetch to confirm.

Meera: I already started (1). Logs will include `selector.reason` and `selected_kernel_hint`.

Nikhil: I can wire up a Datadog query for (kernel_conv_ms median, ttft median) split by `kvcache_prefetch`. Query I used: `median:metric.redwood.token_latency{route:chat-stream,model:rw-v1-13b}.rollup(median,60)` then split by `kvcache_prefetch`.

Ashley: For the dashboard panel, include a small heatmap: x-axis = kernel name, y-axis = ttft buckets, color = counts. Also show per-route pivot.

Meera: Note on sampling: if we upsample more for the impacted route we might see the regression go away (sampling noise). But the traces indicate a real delta.

perf-bot: Deployment: staging/runtime v2.14.3 with instrumentation flags rolled out to 25% at 2026-03-18T10:12:00Z :rocket:

Tom: Let's capture a couple of quick hypotheses: A) prefetch path selects convolutional microkernel with packing overhead B) kernel selector adds an extra memcpy for KV-prefetch metadata C) weird cache line contention on certain GPU types.

Jordan: I can repro on a p4d-ish staging node with synthetic short prompts. If it's cache-line related we should see the regression depend on sequence length and batch size.

Meera: I ran sequence-length sweep (1..64) with 1 sample each on staging node: results pasted:```
seq 1: ttft median 33ms (prefetch attempted)
seq 8: ttft median 28ms (prefetch hit)
seq 32: ttft median 26ms
```

Meera: So regression concentrated at seq <= 2.

Nikhil: Suggestion — modify prefetch heuristic to avoid prefetch for seq<=2 and try canary. Should be low risk.

Ashley: This aligns with earlier microkernel amortization behavior: for extremely short sequences the overhead dominates.

Tom: Can we implement a temporary rule in selector: if predicted tokens <=2, force `kvcache.prefetch=none` OR choose fast tiny-kernel?

Meera: Yes I can patch selector to `if predicted_remaining <= 2: skip_prefetch=true`. Will run a 1h canary on staging.

Jordan: Also capture kernel-level histograms for `kernel_conv_ms` and `kernel_pack_ms` to validate packing overhead.

perf-bot: Canary started: selector rule `skip_prefetch` on staging for 10% of traffic at 2026-03-18T10:45:00Z

Nikhil: Preliminary after 30m: median TTFT for short prompts dropped from 33ms -> 27ms in canary. Kernel_conv_ms reduced by ~3ms.

Tom: Great. That points to prefetch overhead being the main culprit. Next steps: 1) merge temp selector guard 2) instrument packing path more, add metric `kernel_pack_ms` 3) long-term: revise prefetch heuristic to be more conservative for tiny sequences or rely on cheap quick-checks.

Meera: I'll open PR for the guard + packing metric. Will also add a small dashboard card in the runtime perf space showing `ttft_median | kernel_conv_median | kernel_pack_median` by route.

Ashley: Can we add an automated regression alert if short-prompt TTFT 90th percentile increases >10% vs baseline? Want to catch this early.

Meera: Yup — will add SLO-based alert on the new panel, target 5% false positive rate.

Jordan: Thanks all — good catch. Small instrumentation change exposed a selector interaction we hadn't seen.

Tom: :thumbsup: please paste PR link here once ready and schedule a short postmortem doc if it ends up touching prod canary later.

Meera: Will do. PR: pending (will post when green).
